principles: Keep restart correctness ledger-first and do not weaken M1 fail-closed behavior.
Represent provider health, throttle, and worker fencing as explicit local control-plane facts that tests can prove.
Treat Authority Server production receipt semantics as out of scope and never use them for completion claims.
drivers: User requested all Autopilot v2 execution-plan content completed until DONE.
Current code already has M1 and dispatch primitives, so the smallest reliable design is additive reuse.
The DONE answer must include a detailed acceptance table with concrete commands and tests.

options.name: A: Add focused Autopilot reliability core plus one dedicated M2-M4 smoke
pros: Smallest product surface that closes documented gaps
Keeps pure state-machine logic easy to test
Avoids real provider cost or flaky live hosts in smoke tests
cons: M4 proves claim/lease/fencing semantics locally rather than launching a large live provider fleet

options.name: B: Rewrite Autopilot run loop into a full live process pool now
pros: Would exercise more end-to-end live runtime behavior
cons: Provider/session limits make tests slow and flaky
Risks replacing proven M1 ledger semantics

chosen: A: Add focused Autopilot reliability core plus one dedicated M2-M4 smoke
rationale: Option A completes the documented control-plane semantics with deterministic tests and keeps live provider/fleet behavior bounded instead of over-expanding this story.

preMortem.scenario: Throttle or health classification masks terminal failures as retryable.
preMortem.trigger: A quota/auth/policy error gets classified with rate-limit terms.
preMortem.consequence: Autopilot waits forever or retries unsafe work.
preMortem.mitigation: Implement explicit terminal categories and adversarial smoke assertions for auth_required, quota_exhausted, terminal_step_error, and policy_blocked.

preMortem.scenario: Parallel workers duplicate a pending step.
preMortem.trigger: Two workers claim the same step without fencing.
preMortem.consequence: M4 multiplies the duplicate-work class this program is meant to prevent.
preMortem.mitigation: Use atomic claim records with ownerWorkerId, leaseId, leaseExpiresAt, and monotonically increasing fencingToken; smoke conflicting and expired commits.

preMortem.trigger: The acceptance table says all of Autopilot v2 is complete without distinguishing local smoke vs live fleet scope.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers/users believe the CLI keeps dead processes alive or has production Authority guarantees.
preMortem.mitigation: Document local restart-safe/control-plane scope, mark M3/M4 as implemented local control-plane capability, and keep external supervisor/Authority claims out.
